question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(110,0.5),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=65).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9641\,$ | $\,0.9649\,$ | $\,0.9656\,$ |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9773\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=110$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =110\cdot 0.5 \\  & =55 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =110\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =55 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(110)(0.5)=55
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(110)(0.5)(1-0.5)=27.5.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(55,27.5).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=65).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=65)≈P(64.5\le Y\le 65.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(64.5\le Y\le 65.5) & =P(\frac{64.5-55}{\sqrt{27.5}}\le Z\le \frac{65.5-55}{\sqrt{27.5}}) \\  & ≈P(1.81\le Z\le 2.00) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.00)-P(Z<1.81) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.00)-P(Z\le 1.81) \\  & =Φ(2.00)-Φ(1.81) \\  & =0.9773-0.9649 \\  & =0.012\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=65)≈0.012.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0124.$
